Tara / Priya / Marissa — attaching a draft response: RI_Privacy_Response_Cyanova_20270916.docx. Below are the highlights and some inline clarifications for Cyanova's legal review. I'm pasting the key Q&A here for quick triage.

Q: Cross-border transfer mechanism for EU->US processing?
A: Redwood supports multiple lawful transfer mechanisms depending on customer scope:
  - Hosted: we rely on SCCs (EU Commission standard contractual clauses) between Cyanova and Redwood, paired with our internal cross-border mapping (we provide a DPF mapping supplement on request).
  - Dedicated/Private: customers can deploy within a VPC region or on-prem; if Cyanova elects Dedicated in an EU region, exports do not occur outside EEA for covered processing. For tenants using Hosted with residency requirements we offer model routing to EU-only regions and gateway controls to constrain token/content egress.

Q: DPA Annex & redlines?
A: We provided a redline template as a PDF (separate attachment DPA_Annex_Redline_v1.pdf). The annex has modular clauses for deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private), KMS options, and subprocessors. We can accept reasonable counter-proposals but will need operational clarifications for BYOK (Private) and support timelines for key rotations.

Q: KMS / BYOK / HSM?
A: Options:
  - Hosted: keys managed by Redwood KMS with customer-managed keys available through our KMS integration (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) for keys at rest. For cryptographic operations in transit we use TLS 1.3 with ephemeral session keys.
  - Dedicated: optional customer-managed KMS; keys stored in the customer's cloud project or dedicated HSM instance.
  - Private (on-prem): customer retains full key custody; Redwood runtime supports local HSM connectors (PKCS#11) and can operate with a customer-supplied KMS.

Q: Logging & retention?
A: Default: request/response logs are retained 30 days for Hosted evaluation accounts; for production customers defaults are configurable via contract (30/90/365 days options). We can enable request token masking, KV-prefix tokenization, and redacted traces for low-retention sensitive paths. Audit logs (admin actions, deployment changes) are retained 365 days by default and delivered via a secure S3 export on request.

Q: Subprocessors & notification?
A: We publish a subprocessors list and notify customers 30 days before adding a new subprocessors for processor-impacting changes. Emergency disclosures for legal orders are handled per our Incident Response and legal disclosure playbook; we provide transcribed notification and take-avoidance options where lawful.

Evidence delivered with workbook: SOC2_TypeII_Redwood_2026.pdf (redacted IA summary available), high-level dataflow diagram (Dataflow_Diagram_Cyanova_Project.png). We can also provide a pen test executive summary under NDA.

Open items for Cyanova legal to confirm:
- Preferred transfer mechanism (SCCs vs. reliance on adequacy)
- Desired retention windows for request logs and admin audit logs
- Whether Cyanova will require BYOK/HSM for the pilot or only for production scope

I'll finalize the workbook answers and add the annex redline by EOD Sep 16.
